title: Hot role: AIOps agents for DevOps
oneliner: Companies are desperate for people who can build AI agents for DevOps: automatic incident detection, self-healing workflows, and observability with tools like Langfuse.
says: Most companies are desperately looking for AIOps agent skills for DevOps: knowing how to build automatic incident detection, how to implement self-healing workflows, and how to implement observability with the help of Langfuse. If you have these skills and experience, you will do very well in this job market.
explained: DevOps is where agents earn trust fastest, because the work is repetitive, measurable, and painful: triaging alerts, correlating logs, restarting failed services. Automatic incident detection finds the problem; self-healing workflows fix the known cases without paging a human; observability - he names Langfuse, a tool for tracing LLM and agent behavior - is what lets you trust and debug the agents doing it.

The self-healing piece deserves respect rather than fear. Done well it handles the boring 80% - restart, scale, rollback - while escalating the genuinely novel 20% to humans, which connects directly to his agent-orchestrator role: someone still owns the agents. For job seekers, this is a concrete, buildable portfolio: a demo that detects a staged incident and heals it is worth more than another chatbot.
takeaway: AIOps is the most concrete agent job market right now: incident detection + self-healing + agent observability is a buildable, demonstrable skill set.
